document_check.note: The document is Luo M, He Z, Cui H, Chen Y-PP, Ward P, ADNI. 'Class activation attention transfer neural networks for MCI conversion prediction', Computers in Biology and Medicine 156 (2023) 106700. It benchmarks source-task attention transfer (CAAT) head-to-head against a baseline 3D CNN, traditional transfer learning and published methods for pMCI versus sMCI, matching the review's 'Luo et al. 2023'.

cited_result: Head-to-head comparison for 3-year pMCI versus sMCI prediction from a single baseline MRI (ADNI, 295 pMCI / 298 sMCI, 5-fold cross-validation). The CAAT ensemble (attention maps transferred from AD vs CN, ADAS-cog and CDR-SB source tasks) reached accuracy 74.61% and AUC 0.780, against 70.84% / 0.758 for the baseline 3D CNN and 73.37% / 0.782 for the 6-Conv transfer-learning ensemble (Tables 3 and 4).
tool_reason: The cited result is the comparative discrimination (ranking) of prognostic deep-learning models predicting later conversion, which PROBAST covers as performance and ranking of models.

domains.rationale: ADNI is an appropriate cohort source, and the benchmark subject lists of Wen et al. were adopted. The paper does not report how participants with less than 36 months of follow-up, reverters or drop-outs were handled, and the near-equal group sizes (298/295) suggest selection that is not described.

domains.rationale: The authors state that the same 5-fold cross-validation was used both to tune and to select models, which biases the reported performance optimistically. The source-task stopping point was also chosen by its usefulness for the target task. The source tasks were trained on ADNI1/ADNI2 images that include MCI subjects, with no statement excluding target-task test-fold subjects. There was no external validation, no calibration, and no statistical test of differences between models.

overall_rationale: The predictors and outcome domains are low and the participants domain is unclear, but the analysis domain is high. By the authors' own account, tuning and model selection used the same 5-fold cross-validation, and the source-task stopping was chosen by target-task benefit. Source-task training data may overlap target-task test subjects, and there was no external validation, calibration or significance testing. The head-to-head gains that support 'improves' are 1 to 4 accuracy points (74.61% against 70.84% to 73.37%) with near-identical AUCs. Differences of that size are within what tuning optimism can produce, so the comparative result is at high risk of bias.

applicability.rationale: ADNI MCI participants with a 36-month conversion definition, matching the review question of conversion prediction; research-cohort selection limits generalisability somewhat.
